opportunity.title: DA01--FY 27 NYH ISCV DATA RECOVERY SERVICES - 1 YEAR ONLY
opportunity.description: Sources Sought for Philips ISCV Radiographic DICOM data recovery for the VA New York Harbor Healthcare System, Manhattan Campus. Two NetGear ReadyNAS 3220 systems failed with loss of both RAID6 volumes (24 SATA disks). Vendor must forensically image disks, restore DICOM studies from 2007 to 2020, deliver recovered data migratable into AGFA Radiology PACS, and securely destroy all VA data with a Certificate of Destruction. Respondents must confirm a Class-10 (ISO 4) clean room, SSAE 18 SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type I and SOC 3 audit compliance, and IACRB Certified Data Recovery Professional credentials. FAR Part 12 commercial procurement, size standard $34 million, period of performance about Dec 1 2026 to Jan 31 2027. The notice states responses will be used to decide whether to set the procurement aside.

rationale.point: Company has no prior VA, DoD, or HHS prime contracts and only state/local projects under $500K, while a large incumbent (Booz Allen Hamilton) holds a $1.36B VA contract (claim 1), indicating intense competition from established primes.

The requirement to handle DICOM data in a closed end-to-end system for FDA regulatory compliance (claim 4) exceeds the company's current capabilities: no facility clearance, no SOC 2 report, and a six-engineer team without demonstrated medical-data infrastructure.

Although the opportunity supports VA's T4NG initiative for IT services like technical support and cyber security (claim 5), the company's past performance is limited to web and data platforms, not medical data recovery or cyber security in a regulated healthcare environment.

risks: Regulatory compliance gap: FDA requirements for DICOM data demand validated, closed-loop systems the company cannot currently provide.
No VA past performance: zero prime contracts with VA, DoD, or HHS reduces credibility for a healthcare data recovery award.
Small team and no facility clearance: six engineers without cleared facilities or SOC 2 cannot meet likely security and infrastructure mandates.
Open competition (no set-aside): the opportunity has no small-business set-aside, favoring large incumbents with proven VA healthcare IT track records.
nextSteps: Pursue teaming arrangements with a prime that holds FDA-compliant DICOM infrastructure and VA healthcare past performance.
Invest in SOC 2 Type II attestation and facility clearance to qualify for future VA medical-data opportunities.
Target smaller VA subcontracting roles or state-level healthcare IT projects to build relevant past performance.
